analyst_view.overall: Second-placed Real Madrid (33 pts, five straight league wins) host Alaves (9th, 16 pts) on Saturday night, and the numbers make Madrid strong favourites with about 3.2 goals. Jose Mourinho's side play PSV in the Champions League on Tuesday, three games in eight days, and he rotated for that game (Bellingham out of the starting side), so some rotation either way is expected; FutbolFantasy rates the Madrid lineup as hard to predict. Rodrygo, Asencio and Endrick are out and Mendy is doubtful; the numbers list no Madrid absentees, but these are long absences already reflected in Madrid's recent games. Quique Sanchez's Alaves beat Deportivo 3-1 last weekend, are without Facundo Garces and Mikel Rodriguez (cruciate ligament injuries, out until April) and have Hugo Novoa doubtful. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 2.5 for Madrid, already raised for Madrid's 17 goals in their last six (+3.3%). Rodrygo and Endrick are out, but they have been out for weeks while Madrid kept scoring, and Mbappe, Bellingham and Valverde are expected to start. Alaves' attack is in decent form (3-1 against Deportivo), so nothing new points either way and I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, already lowered because Alaves have won few corners lately and Madrid have conceded few (-6.1% on Alaves' side). Madrid's possible rotation after PSV changes little for corners, so I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, 2.8 of them for Alaves, already lowered for Madrid's quiet recent record (-6.3%). No referee is named yet and there is no sign of extra tension: Alaves are comfortable mid-table. I stay at 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots, already raised for Madrid's heavy recent shooting (+5.3%). Mourinho's rotation between the PSV game and Alaves may change some names, but Madrid's squad depth (Guler, Diomande, Vinicius competing for places) keeps their output high, so I stay at 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, already lifted for Madrid's sharp recent finishing (49 on target in six, +7.6%). Alaves keep goalkeeper Sivera and their usual back line apart from Garces, a long-term absence. Nothing new, so I stay at about 10.4.
